questions.q: Per this lesson, what distinct question do roles (Chapter 1) answer, as opposed to what tags and policies (Chapters 2-3) answer?
options: Roles decide who can do what; tags and policies decide what gets protected and how
Roles decide what gets protected; tags decide who can do what
Roles and tags answer the exact same question, just with different syntax
Roles only matter for warehouses; tags only matter for columns
questions.explain: The lesson's central framing: who (roles, Chapter 1) and what/how (masking, row policies, secure views, tags — Chapter 2-3) are two separate questions, and neither replaces the other.

questions.q: Why is a single ALTER TAG statement described as 'the scale argument in miniature'?
options: Because one statement protects every column carrying the tag, present and future, without per-column configuration
Because ALTER TAG is the only statement that can be run by ACCOUNTADMIN
Because it only works on exactly five columns at a time
Because it replaces the need for roles entirely
questions.explain: The scale argument is that one tag, bound to a policy once, protects every column that carries it — now and in the future — which is what makes governance practical at an account too large to configure object-by-object.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what does Universal Search illustrate about tags and classification?
options: Tags and classification make data discoverable by meaning (PII, a semantic category, a cost center), not just by name
Universal Search can only find objects that have been explicitly tagged
Universal Search replaces TAG_REFERENCES_ALL_COLUMNS as the only way to query tags
Universal Search is a masking feature, not a discovery feature
questions.explain: Universal Search finds objects by name; the lesson frames tags and classification as extending that same idea to finding data by what it means, not just what it's called.

questions.q: In the three-statement recap code block, which step is described as something that 'only ever has to happen once'?
options: Wiring a masking policy to the tag with ALTER TAG ... SET MASKING POLICY
Creating the tag with CREATE TAG
Applying the tag to a column with ALTER TABLE ... SET TAG
Running SYSTEM$CLASSIFY
questions.explain: Once a masking policy is attached to a tag, every column currently or later tagged with it is protected automatically — so that binding step doesn't need to be repeated per column.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the four things listed in the 'what tags bought you this chapter' recap?
options: Schema-wide classification with SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA tagging an entire schema in one call
Automatic encryption of every tagged column at rest
Automatic backup of every tagged table every night
Free compute credits for tagged warehouses
questions.explain: The four recap items are: one tag/many columns, schema-wide classification, custom discovery, and discoverability by meaning — schema-wide classification via SYSTEM$CLASSIFY_SCHEMA is one of them.
